newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-SOUTH KOREANS MAY ESCAPE SUSPENSION.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-SOUTH KOREANS MAY ESCAPE SUSPENSION.

text.p: The South Korean players involved in a controversial eight-minute mixed doubles match at the world badminton championships earlier this week may escape suspension following an apology.
An uncompetitive match against a fellow South Korean pair ended 15-1 15-1 in favour of Kim Dong-moon and Ra Kyung-min, Olympic gold and silver medallists in Atlanta when playing with other partners.
The case was discussed by the International Badminton Federation's (IBF) Council on Saturday.

All they would say on Sunday was that they had written to the South Koreans and awaited their reply. But it was believed that a public apology issued the day after the match from the South Korean team manager, who described the players as behaving "irresponsibly," may have taken the heat out of the situation and the quartet may escape with small fines.
Kim and Ra, who were unseeded because they were a new partnership, were knocked out of the tournament the following day.
